title: Environments
bigQuestion: How can we explore and protect the environments around us?
summary: Students learn words for places in nature, directions and weather, talk about plans and timetables with future forms, make predictions with may / might / could, make adjectives from nouns with -y, and think about climate change.
warmup: What is the most beautiful place in nature you have visited?
Would you like to explore a cave or a castle? Why?
What is the weather usually like in the north and the south of Saudi Arabia?
What are you going to do this weekend?
How can we help to protect our environment?

grammar.title: Talking about the future
grammar.rule: Use be going to for plans you have already made and for things you can see will happen. Use will for quick decisions, offers and promises. Use the Simple Present for timetables (trains, shops, tours), and the Present Progressive for arrangements with a day or time.
grammar.form: plan: am / is / are going to + verb · quick decision / offer: will ('ll) + verb · timetable: Simple Present (opens, leaves) · arrangement: am / is / are + verb-ing + time
examples: We're going to explore the cave this weekend.
Look at those black clouds! It's going to rain.
The museum opens at 10 a.m. tomorrow.
We're flying to Abha on Thursday.
Your bag looks heavy. I'll carry it for you.

items.prompt: The old fort ___ at 8 a.m. every day, so we can visit it tomorrow morning.
items.explanation: Opening times are a timetable, so we use the Simple Present: opens.

items.prompt: Look at those dark clouds! It ___ rain.
items.explanation: We can see the clouds, so we use is going to for the prediction.

items.prompt: A: This bag is very heavy! B: ___
options: I carried it for you yesterday.
items.explanation: For a quick offer, we use will ('ll) + verb.

items.prompt: We ___ the train to Jeddah tomorrow. Dad bought the tickets yesterday.
items.explanation: It is an arrangement with a time, so we use the Present Progressive: are taking.

items.prompt: What time ___ the bus leave tomorrow?
items.explanation: Bus times are a timetable, so we use the Simple Present: does the bus leave.

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: I'm going to visit the cave next week.
I going to visit the cave next week.
I'm go to visit the cave next week.
items.answer: I'm going to visit the cave next week.
items.explanation: Be going to needs am / is / are + going to + verb.

items.prompt: Nouf ___ going to climb the hill on Saturday.
items.explanation: Nouf is one person, so we use is going to.

items.prompt: We ___ going to explore the cave this weekend.
items.explanation: With we, the form is are going to.

items.prompt: Be careful! You ___ going to fall into the stream!
items.explanation: We can see it will happen, so we use are going to with you.

items.prompt: The train to Dammam ___ at 7:30 tomorrow morning.
items.explanation: Train times are a timetable, so the Simple Present leaves is best.

items.prompt: A: I'm thirsty. B: Wait, ___ get you some water.
items.explanation: B decides to help right now, so we use will ('ll).

items.prompt: Don't worry, Mom. I promise I ___ be late.
items.explanation: For promises we use will. The negative is won't / will not.

items.prompt: What time ___ the castle close tonight?
items.explanation: Closing times are a timetable, so we ask with does.

items.prompt: Nouf ___ a party next Thursday. She has invited ten friends.
items.explanation: It is a plan with a day, so we use is having (or is going to have).

items.prompt: Omar ___ his grandfather in AlUla tomorrow. He has his plane ticket.
items.explanation: It is an arrangement for tomorrow, so we use is visiting (or is going to visit).

items.answer: We are going to cross the bridge.
items.explanation: Subject + are going to + verb.

items.answer: The boat leaves at six tomorrow.
alt: Tomorrow the boat leaves at six.
The boat leaves tomorrow at six.
items.explanation: Timetables use the Simple Present: the boat leaves.

items.answer: I will carry your bag for you.
items.explanation: An offer: I will + verb.

items.answer: Are you meeting your cousins on Friday?
items.explanation: Present Progressive question: Are + you + verb-ing.

items.answer: It is going to be a great adventure!
items.explanation: It is going to + be + adjective + noun.

items.prompt: Sara is going to visit the cave.
answer: Is Sara going to visit the cave?

items.prompt: The bus will stop at the bridge.

items.explanation: Simple Present question: What time + does + subject + verb?

items.sentence: The plane is leave at 8 p.m. tomorrow.

items.sentence: I'll open the window for you.
items.answer: I'll open the window for you.

items.sentence: We are visit our grandparents next weekend.
items.answer: We are visiting our grandparents next weekend.

grammar.title: Predictions with may, might, could
grammar.rule: Use may, might or could + verb when something is possible, but you are not sure. They all mean 'maybe'. For the negative, use may not or might not.
grammar.form: subject + may / might / could + verb · subject + may not / might not + verb
examples: The cave may be very dark, so bring a flashlight.
We could get lost without a guide.
There might be a storm tonight.
Reem might not come with us.

items.prompt: Take a coat. It ___ be cold on the hill.
items.explanation: Might never changes, and it is followed by a verb without to.

items.prompt: We could ___ lost in the fog.
items.explanation: After could we use the base verb: get.

items.prompt: The stream ___ not be deep. Let's check.
items.explanation: May not + verb shows we are not sure.

items.prompt: Which sentence means "Maybe there will be a storm"?
items.explanation: Might means maybe, so it shows something is possible.

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
items.explanation: May + base verb, with no -s and no to.

items.prompt: I'm not sure, but Omar ___ come to the castle with us.
items.explanation: Could + verb shows it is possible.

items.prompt: Bring a flashlight. The cave ___ be very dark.
items.explanation: We are not sure, so we use may, might or could.

items.prompt: Don't stand near the edge. You ___ fall!
items.explanation: It is possible, so we use might, may or could.

items.prompt: The sky is clear. It ___ rain today.
items.explanation: For a negative prediction we use may not or might not.

items.prompt: We might ___ a boat to cross the river.
items.explanation: After might we use the base verb: need.

items.prompt: Fahad isn't sure. He ___ go to the beach this weekend, or he might stay home.
items.explanation: He isn't sure, so we use may, might or could.

items.prompt: Take some water. The walk to the castle could ___ very long.
items.explanation: After could we use the base verb: be.

items.prompt: Nouf doesn't like walking. She ___ enjoy the hiking trip.
items.explanation: For a negative prediction we use may not or might not.

items.prompt: There ___ be fog on the bridge tonight, so please drive slowly, Dad.
items.explanation: We are not sure about the fog, so we use may, might or could.
Subject + might + be + adjective.

items.answer: We could get lost in the cave.
items.explanation: Subject + could + base verb.

items.answer: The bridge may not be safe.
items.explanation: Negative: may + not + base verb.

items.answer: There might be a storm tonight.
alt: Tonight there might be a storm.
items.explanation: There + might + be + noun.

items.answer: The stream might be too deep.
items.explanation: Subject + might + be + too + adjective.

items.prompt: Maybe it will rain this afternoon.
items.explanation: Might + base verb has the same meaning as maybe ... will.

items.prompt: Perhaps the castle is closed today.
answer: The castle may be closed today.
items.explanation: Is becomes may be.

items.prompt: Maybe Reem won't come to the cave.
answer: Reem might not come to the cave.
Reem mightn't come to the cave.
items.explanation: Won't come becomes might not come.

items.prompt: Maybe we will see dolphins in the ocean.
answer: We could see dolphins in the ocean.
items.explanation: Could + base verb shows it is possible.
After might, use the base verb with no -s.

items.sentence: We may to need a boat.
items.explanation: Don't use to after may.

items.sentence: The path could be dangerous in the dark.
items.answer: The path could be dangerous in the dark.
items.explanation: Correct: could + be shows something is possible.
Might never takes -s.

reading.title: Lost in the Fog
reading.text:
Last spring, Reem's family went on an adventure in the mountains near Abha. On the first morning, their guide, Uncle Saad, met them at the hotel. "We're going to walk to an old stone castle on the hill," he said. "Listen carefully. The weather here changes quickly. It might get foggy, so stay on the path and stay together."

First, they walked along a small stream. Then they crossed a wooden bridge and turned left at a big stone. After an hour, they saw the castle. It had high walls and a dark tower. Reem took lots of photos.

Suddenly, thick fog came down from the hills. Reem couldn't see her little brother, Khalid! She called his name, but there was no answer. Then she remembered Uncle Saad's words. "Stay on the path!" she shouted. A minute later, Khalid answered. He was standing on the path, just a few meters away.

Uncle Saad led everyone back slowly. That evening, Reem said, "I'm glad we listened to you. Next time, I'll listen even more carefully!"

questions.prompt: Where did Reem's family go?
questions.explanation: The story says they went to the mountains near Abha.

They went back to the hotel.

questions.explanation: They crossed the bridge and then turned left at a big stone.
The story says it had high walls and a dark tower.

questions.statement: Khalid was lost in a cave.
questions.explanation: Khalid was on the path in the fog, not in a cave.

questions.explanation: He said, "stay on the path and stay together."

questions.prompt: What did Reem learn?
options: It is important to listen to others.
questions.answer: It is important to listen to others.
questions.explanation: She is glad they listened, and she will listen more carefully next time.

reading.title: Our Changing Planet
reading.text:
Our planet is getting warmer. This is called climate change. Cars, factories and power stations put gases into the air. These gases act like a blanket around the Earth and keep the heat in.

Scientists say climate change could change many environments. The ice in the north and the south of the world is melting, so the oceans are getting higher. In the future, some beaches and islands might disappear under the water. There may also be more storms, and some hot places could get even hotter and drier. Animals and plants might lose their homes.

The good news is that we can help. Saudi Arabia is planting millions of trees to make the air cleaner. NEOM is going to use energy from the sun and the wind. You can help too. Walk or cycle when you can. Turn off the lights when you leave a room. Don't waste water.

If we all make small changes, our planet will be a better place for people, animals and plants. What are you going to do to help?

questions.explanation: The article explains climate change and how we can help.

questions.explanation: The article says the gases act like a blanket and keep the heat in.

questions.explanation: The article says the ice in the north and south is melting.

questions.explanation: The ice is melting, so the oceans are getting higher.

questions.explanation: NEOM is going to use energy from the sun and the wind.

reading.title: Into the Cave!
reading.text:
Hi everyone, it's Omar! This weekend, my family and I are going on a real adventure. We're going to explore a cave in the desert north of Riyadh.

Here is our plan. We're leaving home on Friday at six in the morning. The tour starts at eight o'clock, and it finishes at noon. Our guide is meeting us at the entrance.

My dad says the cave is very deep. Some parts are more than one hundred meters under the ground! It may be very dark inside, so I'm going to bring two flashlights. There might be bats on the high stone walls. My little sister is a bit scared, so I told her, "Don't worry. I'll hold your hand."

The air inside the cave could be cold, even in summer, so Mom is packing jackets for everyone. The path into the cave is narrow and rocky, so we're going to wear strong shoes.

At the bottom, there is a small lake with clear blue water. I might take photos of it, but my camera might not work well in the dark.

I'll write another post next week with my photos. What do you think we will find down there?

questions.prompt: When does the cave tour start?
questions.explanation: Omar writes, "The tour starts at eight o'clock."

questions.explanation: Omar says it may be very dark, so he is going to bring two flashlights.

questions.explanation: Omar says the air inside the cave could be cold, even in summer.

options: Maybe there are bats, but Omar isn't sure.
questions.answer: Maybe there are bats, but Omar isn't sure.
questions.explanation: Might means maybe: Omar thinks bats are possible, but he is not sure.

questions.prompt: Mom is packing ___ for everyone because the air could be cold.
questions.explanation: The blog says Mom is packing jackets for everyone.

questions.prompt: What promise did Omar make to his little sister?
questions.explanation: Omar told her, "Don't worry. I'll hold your hand." We use will for promises.

reading.title: Our Trip to the Red Sea
reading.text:
Al-Yasmin Girls' School Newsletter

Next Tuesday, all Grade 6 students are visiting a marine center on the Red Sea coast, south of Jeddah. Here is everything you need to know.

The bus leaves the school at 7:30 a.m. and arrives at the center at about 9:00. Please don't be late, because the bus won't wait!

In the morning, a scientist is giving us a talk about the ocean. She is going to show us how coral reefs grow. Then we are taking a glass-bottom boat out to the reef. The water there isn't very deep, so we will see fish, turtles and maybe even a dolphin!

The weather report says it might be windy in the afternoon. There may also be a storm in the evening, but we will be back at school by 3:00 p.m. If the waves are too high, we could visit the aquarium instead of going on the boat trip.

Please bring a hat, sunscreen, water and lunch. The sun on the coast is very strong, and the air is hot and humid.

Our science teacher, Ms. Huda, says, "This trip is going to be an amazing adventure. Our students will learn how to protect the ocean."

questions.explanation: The newsletter says the bus leaves the school at 7:30 a.m.

questions.explanation: The marine center is on the Red Sea coast, south of Jeddah.

questions.explanation: The newsletter says she is going to show them how coral reefs grow.

reading.title: Storm on Camp Night
reading.text:
Khalid and his cousin Fahad were very excited. Their fathers were taking them camping near the Tuwaiq hills, west of Riyadh.

In the afternoon, the boys climbed a small hill and looked around. In the east, they could see the city. In the west, big black clouds were coming. "Look at those clouds!" said Fahad's father. "There's going to be a storm. We may need to leave our tent."

Khalid's father checked the map. "There is a cave about five hundred meters to the north," he said. "It could be safer than the tent. Follow the path, and turn right at the old tree."

They packed quickly. While they were walking, the wind got stronger, and sand filled the air. Khalid held Fahad's arm. "Don't let go," he said. "I won't," said Fahad.

Ten minutes later, they reached the cave. It wasn't very deep, but it was dry. The storm lasted for an hour. Outside, rain fell and the dark sky flashed. Inside, the boys ate dates, drank tea and told stories by the light of a flashlight.

The next morning, the air was fresh and clean. "That was the best adventure ever," said Khalid. "Next time, we'll check the weather first!"

wordWork.title: Suffixes: making adjectives from nouns
wordWork.rule: We can add -y to many weather and nature nouns to make adjectives: storm → stormy, cloud → cloudy. Some short words double the last letter (fog → foggy, sun → sunny). Other suffixes are -ful (help → helpful) and -ous (danger → dangerous).

items.prompt: There is a lot of fog today. It is ___.
items.explanation: Fog + -y = foggy. We double the g.

items.prompt: There is a storm tonight. It is a ___ night.
items.explanation: Storm + -y = stormy.

items.prompt: The sun is shining. It's a ___ day!
items.explanation: Sun + -y = sunny. We double the n.

items.prompt: There is a lot of wind. It is ___.
items.explanation: Wind + -y = windy.

items.prompt: The path has lots of rocks. It is ___.
items.explanation: Rock + -y = rocky.

items.prompt: The sky is full of clouds. It's ___.
items.explanation: Cloud + -y = cloudy.

items.prompt: Swimming in a storm is not safe. It is ___.
items.explanation: Danger + -ous = dangerous.

items.prompt: Uncle Saad gave us lots of help. He was very ___.
items.explanation: Help + -ful = helpful.

items.prompt: It's snowing in Tabuk! The mountains are ___.
items.explanation: Snow + -y = snowy.

items.prompt: Which noun + suffix is correct?
items.explanation: Fog ends in one vowel + one consonant, so we double the g: foggy.

writing.prompt: Write a short article about climate change. What might happen in the future, and what are you going to do to help?
writing.hint: Use may / might / could for predictions and going to / will for plans.
writing.model: Climate change is a big problem. In the future, summers might get hotter, and there could be more storms. Some animals may lose their homes. I want to help, so I am going to walk to my friend's house instead of going by car. I will turn off the lights when I leave a room. Small changes can help our planet.

writing.prompt: Write directions from your school to a place in nature or an old building. What will people see on the way?
writing.hint: Use turn left, turn right, bridge, path, hill, north, south, east, west.
writing.model: Start at the school gate and walk north. Turn left at the mosque and walk along the path next to the stream. Cross the small bridge. Then turn right and go up the hill. At the top of the hill, you will see an old stone castle. Be careful, because the path could be rocky.
